fed.probabilities_note: Market-implied Fed path, read from the curve instead of the licensed CME futures feed: the gap between the 1-year Treasury and the current target midpoint. Positive = easing priced, negative = tightening priced. A real signal, not an option-implied probability.
fed.caveat: The Fed does not set mortgage rates. It moves the front end; mortgage rates follow the 10Y and the MBS spread.

bullets.text: 10-year Treasury at 5.00%, +4 bp on the day. This is the single biggest input to your rate.
Published 30-year survey at 7.32%, -8 bp week over week. It is a weekly average and always lags your rate sheet.
Mortgage spread 236 bp, normal at the 69th percentile of 10 years. That is 2.36 points of the 7.32% rate coming from spread, not from Treasuries.
Brent Crude $-3.60, bigger than 93% of moves on record. Watch whether the bond market trades this as inflation or as demand.

why.headline: Mortgage rates are under upward pressure. The 10-year Treasury is 5.00% (+4 bp on the day) and the modeled 30-year sits near 7.36%.
why.summary: The 10-year Treasury is at 5.00%, +4 bp on the day. Mortgage rates take their direction from the 10-year first. Between the last two published mortgage surveys the 30-year moved -8 bp. That breaks down exactly: -14 bp from Treasuries and +6 bp from the mortgage spread. The mortgage/10-year spread is 236 bp, which is normal and sits at the 69th percentile of the last 10 years. The long-run average is 208 bp, so roughly 28 bp of the current mortgage rate is spread rather than Treasury yield. Intraday spread movement is not observable here. Without a live MBS feed the daily read assumes the spread held and moves the rate with the 10-year only.

contributions.label: Retail sales
contributions.chain: Retail sales → ↑ Growth expectations → ↑ 10Y Treasury → ↑ MBS yield → ↑ 30Y mortgage rate
rationales: MBS are priced off the Treasury curve. This is the main channel.
Lenders price off MBS execution, with a short lag for rate sheets.

rationales: Brent prices roughly two thirds of the world’s traded crude, so it is the better read on GLOBAL inflation. Foreign inflation feeds foreign policy rates, which feeds the demand for US duration.
The 10Y is a real yield plus an inflation expectation. Expectations move the nominal.

legs.rationale: Brent prices roughly two thirds of the world’s traded crude, so it is the better read on GLOBAL inflation. Foreign inflation feeds foreign policy rates, which feeds the demand for US duration.

legs.chain: Brent crude (global benchmark) → ↑ Recession risk → ↓ 10Y Treasury → ↓ MBS yield → ↓ 30Y mortgage rate
legs.rationale: A sustained crude spike is a tax on the consumer. This is the offsetting channel: the same oil move that lifts inflation expectations also raises recession risk, and those two push mortgage rates in opposite directions.

contributions.self_offset_note: Brent crude (global benchmark) reaches mortgage rates through 2 competing channels, so the net (-0.20) is smaller than either leg. -0.40 via Inflation expectations vs +0.19 via Recession risk

brief.title: MORTGAGE MARKET MORNING BRIEF
brief.body: Mortgage rates: 7.32% published 2026-10-22, modeled 7.36% today. 10-year Treasury: 5.00% (+4 bp). MBS: -5.40 ticks. Rate bias: Worsening. The mortgage spread is 236 bp, normal versus its 208 bp long-run average. Ahead: Core PCE Price Index on 10-28. Biggest risk: Core PCE Price Index. A hot print reverses any Treasury rally. What LOs should know: protect anything closing inside 30 days and expect reprice risk intraday
